text:
title: Configuration Item (CI) Identification Process
lanes: CM, Systems Engineering, Supporting Functions, Program Management, Acquirer

# Inputs. Each function maintains its own products. CM reads them.
start -> fork 1
fork 1 -> Systems Engineering: Maintain architecture and decomposition -> join 1
fork 1 -> Supporting Functions: Maintain hazard, criticality, and support analyses -> join 1
fork 1 -> Acquirer: Set contract and directed CIs -> join 1

# Candidate CI identification and selection. CM decides.
join 1 -> CM: Nominate candidate CIs from source material -> Pass the three qualifying gates?
Pass the three qualifying gates? -yes-> Run criteria screen (a) to (g)
Pass the three qualifying gates? -no-> Record do-not-designate rationale and parent CI
Run criteria screen (a) to (g) -> Supporting Functions: Concur on technical basis -> CM: Any criterion met?
Any criterion met? -no-> Record do-not-designate rationale and parent CI -> Build CI structure and boundary set
Any criterion met? -yes-> Designate CI and record rationale

# CI structure and interfaces. CM owns coverage. Systems Engineering owns content.
Designate CI and record rationale -> Build CI structure and boundary set -> Systems Engineering: Identify interface requirements -> CM: Record interface register and verify coverage

# Acquirer review and concurrence
Record interface register and verify coverage -> Program Management: Approve CI list for submittal -> CM: Submit CI list with rationale -> Acquirer: Acquirer concurs?
Acquirer concurs? ..no, revise..> Run criteria screen (a) to (g)

# Identifiers, documentation, and baselines
Acquirer concurs? -yes-> CM: Assign identifiers -> Determine configuration documentation -> Establish baselines and record in CSA -> Re-evaluation trigger?

# Maintenance and iteration
Re-evaluation trigger? ..yes, re-run..> Nominate candidate CIs from source material
Re-evaluation trigger? -no-> end
